title: Lunchtime dilemma
titleChinese: 午饭时间的“选择困难症”
paragraphs: Whether at school, college or work, most of us take some sort of lunch break. It‘s a good time to have a rest, catch up with friends and eat some food - but here lies the dilemma - what to eat? There are a feast of options but because of limited time or money, many of us stick to what we know - usually the humble sandwich.

Some of us make our own sandwiches in the morning before heading out, whilst those in a rush tend to grab-and-go at a snack bar or a cafe or buy a meal deal at a supermarket. A packet of crisps may be an additional staple to our predictable lunch. What we eat is usually the same everyday. Sheila Dillon from the BBC Food Programme says more than a third of office workers have eaten the same midday meal for the last nine months.

In the UK, bread has become the mainstay of our lunchtime snack, sometimes eaten at your desk - a style known as ’al-desko‘. Bread is cheap and fills you up and with average lunch hours now reduced to 25 minutes, 24 seconds, it‘s quick and convenient to eat. But it's also boring! Some people have broken the mould by bringing in leftovers from their previous night‘s dinner, which they then heat up in a microwave but even that isn't very exciting.

We are creatures of habit but philosopher Julian Baggini says “we‘re never going to break out of our midday malaise unless we think outside the box.” There are alternatives that will fill you up. With just a microwave and a kettle, there are a number of hot satisfying meals than can be made such as soups and jacket potatoes served with a dollop of baked beans or cheese. And then there are the ubiquitous instant noodles in a pot - although you may question how nutritious they are.

If you‘ve got time for more exotic munchies, then look out for trendy ’Ottolenghi‘ style food such as fava bean salad wrap. There is also the healthy Japanese style ’bento box‘ or lunchbox that normally contains a mix of carbohydrate, protein and vegetable. And of course another healthy Japanese treat is sushi.

But if I’ve got time for a proper lunch, I head to my local greasy spoon and tuck into a fry-up. Not very healthy but delicious and it sets me up for an afternoon of hard work. Then it‘s time for the next dilemma - what to have for dinner?! What do you usually eat for lunch?

vocabulary.entry: dilemma [n.] /dɪˈlemə/ 两难境地；进退两难的困境
vocabulary.example: She faced the dilemma of whether to stay or leave.
vocabulary.translation: 她面临留下还是离开的两难境地。

vocabulary.entry: feast [n.] /fiːst/ 盛宴；丰富的数量
vocabulary.example: There is a feast of entertainment options in the city.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市有丰富多样的娱乐选择。

vocabulary.entry: grab-and-go [adj.] /ˌɡræb ən ˈɡəʊ/ 买了就走的；可带走的
vocabulary.example: The café offers grab-and-go sandwiches for busy customers.
vocabulary.translation: 这家咖啡馆为忙碌的顾客提供可带走的方便三明治。

vocabulary.entry: crisps [n. pl.] /krɪsps/ 薯片 (英式英语)
vocabulary.example: He opened a packet of crisps and started eating.
vocabulary.translation: 他打开一包薯片开始吃。

vocabulary.entry: staple [n.] /ˈsteɪpəl/ 主食；主要部分
vocabulary.example: Rice is a staple food in many Asian countries.
vocabulary.translation: 大米是许多亚洲国家的主食。

vocabulary.entry: mainstay [n.] /ˈmeɪnsteɪ/ 主要依靠；支柱
vocabulary.example: Tourism is the mainstay of the local economy.
vocabulary.translation: 旅游业是当地经济的支柱。

vocabulary.entry: al-desko [adv.] /æl ˈdeskəʊ/ 在办公桌旁（用餐）(新词；幽默用法)
vocabulary.example: Many office workers eat lunch al-desko.
vocabulary.translation: 许多上班族在办公桌旁吃午餐。

vocabulary.entry: break the mould [phr.] /breɪk ðə məʊld/ 打破常规；打破模式
vocabulary.example: The new design breaks the mould of traditional architecture.
vocabulary.translation: 这个新设计打破了传统建筑的常规。

vocabulary.entry: leftovers [n. pl.] /ˈleftəʊvəz/ 剩菜；剩饭
vocabulary.example: We had leftovers from yesterday‘s dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 我们吃了昨晚的剩菜。

vocabulary.entry: malaise [n.] /məˈleɪz/ 不适；萎靡不振 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He felt a sense of malaise after working long hours.
vocabulary.translation: 长时间工作后，他感到一种萎靡不振。

vocabulary.entry: think outside the box [phr.] /θɪŋk ˌaʊtˈsaɪd ðə ˈbɒks/ 跳出常规思维
vocabulary.example: We need to think outside the box to solve this problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要跳出常规思维来解决这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: jacket potato [n.] /ˌdʒækɪt pəˈteɪtəʊ/ 带皮烤土豆
vocabulary.example: She ordered a jacket potato with cheese and beans.
vocabulary.translation: 她点了一份带奶酪和焗豆的带皮烤土豆。

vocabulary.entry: dollop [n.] /ˈdɒləp/ 一大块；一团 (食物)
vocabulary.example: He added a dollop of cream to his coffee.
vocabulary.translation: 他在咖啡里加了一大块奶油。

vocabulary.entry: ubiquitous [adj.] /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/ 无处不在的；普遍存在的
vocabulary.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
vocabulary.translation: 智能手机在日常生活中已经无处不在。

vocabulary.entry: instant noodles [n. pl.] /ˌɪnstənt ˈnuːdəlz/ 方便面；即食面
vocabulary.example: Students often eat instant noodles as a quick meal.
vocabulary.translation: 学生们经常吃方便面作为快餐。

vocabulary.entry: nutritious [adj.] /njuːˈtrɪʃəs/ 有营养的；营养丰富的
vocabulary.example: A nutritious breakfast gives you energy for the day.
vocabulary.translation: 一顿营养丰富的早餐为你提供一天的能量。

vocabulary.entry: exotic [adj.] /ɪɡˈzɒtɪk/ 异国风味的；奇异的
vocabulary.example: She enjoys trying exotic foods when she travels.
vocabulary.translation: 她旅行时喜欢尝试异国风味的食物。

vocabulary.entry: munchies [n. pl.] /ˈmʌntʃiz/ 小吃；零食 (口语)
vocabulary.example: We bought some munchies for the movie night.
vocabulary.translation: 我们为电影之夜买了一些零食。

vocabulary.entry: bento box [n.] /ˈbentəʊ bɒks/ 便当盒 (日语借词)
vocabulary.example: She packed a bento box for her lunch.
vocabulary.translation: 她为午餐打包了一个便当盒。

vocabulary.entry: carbohydrate [n.] /ˌkɑːbəʊˈhaɪdreɪt/ 碳水化合物
vocabulary.example: Bread and pasta are rich in carbohydrates.
vocabulary.translation: 面包和意大利面富含碳水化合物。

vocabulary.entry: protein [n.] /ˈprəʊtiːn/ 蛋白质
vocabulary.example: Meat and beans are good sources of protein.
vocabulary.translation: 肉类和豆类是蛋白质的良好来源。

vocabulary.entry: greasy spoon [n.] /ˌɡriːsi ˈspuːn/ 廉价小餐馆 (口语)
vocabulary.example: We had breakfast at a greasy spoon near the station.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在车站附近的一家廉价小餐馆吃了早餐。

vocabulary.entry: tuck into [phr.] /tʌk ˈɪntə/ 痛快地吃；尽情地吃 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The children tucked into the pizza hungrily.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们狼吞虎咽地吃起了披萨。

vocabulary.entry: fry-up [n.] /ˈfraɪ ʌp/ 油炸食物拼盘 (英式英语；口语)
vocabulary.example: He ordered a full English fry-up for breakfast.
vocabulary.translation: 他早餐点了一份全英式油炸食物拼盘。

vocabulary.entry: set someone up for [phr.] /set ˈsʌmwʌn ʌp fɔː/ 为……做好准备
vocabulary.example: A good breakfast sets you up for the day.
vocabulary.translation: 一顿好的早餐为你一天做好准备。

sentences.english: Whether at school, college or work, most of us take some sort of lunch break.
sentences.chinese: 无论是在学校、大学还是工作中，我们大多数人都会有某种形式的午休时间。

sentences.english: It‘s a good time to have a rest, catch up with friends and eat some food - but here lies the dilemma - what to eat?
sentences.chinese: 这是一个休息、和朋友聊聊天以及吃点东西的好时机——但这里存在一个两难境地——吃什么呢？

sentences.english: There are a feast of options but because of limited time or money, many of us stick to what we know - usually the humble sandwich.
sentences.chinese: 选择可谓丰富多样，但由于有限的时间或金钱，我们很多人还是继续选择我们熟悉的食物——通常就是简单的三明治。

sentences.english: Some of us make our own sandwiches in the morning before heading out, whilst those in a rush tend to grab-and-go at a snack bar or a cafe or buy a meal deal at a supermarket.
sentences.chinese: 我们中的一些人会在早上出门前自己制作三明治，而那些匆忙的人则倾向于在小吃店或咖啡馆买了就走，或者在超市购买套餐。

sentences.english: A packet of crisps may be an additional staple to our predictable lunch.
sentences.chinese: 一包薯片可能是我们可以预见的午餐中额外的主食。

sentences.english: What we eat is usually the same everyday.
sentences.chinese: 我们每天吃的东西通常都是一样的。

sentences.english: Sheila Dillon from the BBC Food Programme says more than a third of office workers have eaten the same midday meal for the last nine months.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司美食节目的希拉·狄龙说，在过去的九个月里，超过三分之一的上班族每天吃的午餐都是一样的。

sentences.english: In the UK, bread has become the mainstay of our lunchtime snack, sometimes eaten at your desk - a style known as ’al-desko‘.
sentences.chinese: 在英国，面包已经成为我们午间快餐的主要部分，有时人们会在办公桌前吃——这种方式被称为“在办公桌旁用餐”。

sentences.english: Bread is cheap and fills you up and with average lunch hours now reduced to 25 minutes, 24 seconds, it‘s quick and convenient to eat.
sentences.chinese: 面包价格便宜，能让你吃饱，而且现在平均午餐时间缩短到了25分钟24秒，吃起来又快又方便。

sentences.english: But it's also boring!
sentences.chinese: 但它也很无趣！

sentences.english: Some people have broken the mould by bringing in leftovers from their previous night‘s dinner, which they then heat up in a microwave but even that isn't very exciting.
sentences.chinese: 一些人打破了这种模式，把前一晚晚餐的剩菜带来，然后用微波炉加热，但即便如此也不是很令人兴奋。

sentences.english: We are creatures of habit but philosopher Julian Baggini says “we‘re never going to break out of our midday malaise unless we think outside the box.”
sentences.chinese: 我们是习惯的产物，但哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼说：“除非我们跳出常规思维，否则我们永远无法摆脱中午的这种不适状态。”

sentences.english: There are alternatives that will fill you up.
sentences.chinese: 还有其他能让你吃饱的选择。

sentences.english: With just a microwave and a kettle, there are a number of hot satisfying meals than can be made such as soups and jacket potatoes served with a dollop of baked beans or cheese.
sentences.chinese: 只要有一个微波炉和一个水壶，就可以做出许多令人满足的热食，比如汤和烤土豆，再配上一大块焗豆或奶酪。

sentences.english: And then there are the ubiquitous instant noodles in a pot - although you may question how nutritious they are.
sentences.chinese: 然后还有无处不在的即食泡面——尽管你可能会质疑它们的营养价值。

sentences.english: If you‘ve got time for more exotic munchies, then look out for trendy ’Ottolenghi‘ style food such as fava bean salad wrap.
sentences.chinese: 如果你有时间享用更异国风味的小吃，那就留意一下时尚的“奥托伦吉”风格的食物，比如蚕豆沙拉卷。

sentences.english: There is also the healthy Japanese style ’bento box‘ or lunchbox that normally contains a mix of carbohydrate, protein and vegetable.
sentences.chinese: 还有健康的日式“便当盒”，通常里面包含碳水化合物、蛋白质和蔬菜的混合搭配。

sentences.english: And of course another healthy Japanese treat is sushi.
sentences.chinese: 当然，另一种健康的日式美食就是寿司。

sentences.english: But if I’ve got time for a proper lunch, I head to my local greasy spoon and tuck into a fry-up.
sentences.chinese: 但如果我有时间吃一顿像样的午餐，我会去当地的廉价小餐馆，尽情享用一顿油炸食物。

sentences.english: Not very healthy but delicious and it sets me up for an afternoon of hard work.
sentences.chinese: 虽然不是很健康，但很美味，而且能让我为一下午的辛勤工作做好准备。

sentences.english: Then it‘s time for the next dilemma - what to have for dinner?!
sentences.chinese: 然后就到了下一个两难境地——晚餐吃什么呢？！

sentences.english: What do you usually eat for lunch?
sentences.chinese: 你通常午餐吃什么呢？
